Three things are needed before the day, and each ends in something that you can check: R and the workspace installed, with the setup check printing OK; the first module on R worked through; and the case study read. The modules on the IDE, on Quarto and on Git and GitHub are recommended for anyone who would rather meet the tools at their own pace than on the day. The day itself is worked mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser with the data already in place, so a machine on which the installation failed can still follow every task.

## 1. R and the workspace

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace zip, and run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK. You do this once, and the workspace is yours to keep after the day. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. If the installation will not cooperate, tell the facilitator before the day, and follow the day in the browser lab.

## 2. Getting started with R

[Open Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The module teaches the R that the browser lab asks of you, from a first line of code to a share of replies, a difference between two shares, a table and a figure, all on the data of this case. Its blocks of code run in your browser, so it can be worked before the installation, alongside it, or on a machine on which you cannot install anything.

## 3. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study and its design, SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the question that each of them answered, how their results were put on one scale, and the replication with new data. Every part of the day works on this case.

## 4. The browser lab

[Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Open the lab once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the first cell shows a "Run Code" button, and run the setup cell of Task 1. If it does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the day.

## 5. Further preparation

The modules on [the IDE (Positron and other IDEs)](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), on [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and on [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) take the tools of the workspace further, each with tasks in the workspace of this case. The [exercise overview](../../cases/housing/exercise.qmd) sets out the claim that you will be working on, the five tasks, and the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found when they reanalysed it.

**By the start of the day** you have the setup check printing OK, or the browser lab loading on the machine that you will use, you have worked through the first module on R, and you know what the claim is and how the five Multi100 analysts came to different conclusions about it.
